subject: Racial Equity and West Medford Leadership
overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed Chelli Keshavan regarding her new roles with the Human Rights Commission and the West Medford Community Center. The discussion focused on preserving the historical identity of West Medford, addressing housing affordability, and expanding racial justice and maternal health initiatives in the city.

items.title: Chamber of Commerce Local Business Promotion
items.summary: Balocca announced a February loyalty card program incentivizing residents to shop at local businesses for a chance to win tickets and cash.

items.title: Introduction and Professional Background
items.summary: Chelli Keshavan introduced her work in maternal health equity and her leadership roles with the Medford Human Rights Commission and the West Medford Community Center.

items.title: Local Restaurant Recommendation
items.summary: Keshavan identified the Brazilian Steakhouse as a significant local institution and her favorite place to dine in the city.

items.title: West Medford History and Property Retention
items.summary: The discussion explored West Medford's legacy as a middle-class Black neighborhood and the importance of preserving intergenerational wealth and community culture.

items.title: Diversity versus Pro-Black Policy
items.summary: Keshavan analyzed the distinction between generic diversity initiatives and specific pro-Black municipal policies in the wake of COVID-19 and racial reckoning.

items.title: Housing Affordability and Education
items.summary: Speakers addressed how high housing costs impact family retention and the demographic makeup of Medford Public Schools.

items.title: Human Rights Commission Strategic Goals
items.summary: Keshavan outlined her intention to lead the commission with needs assessments, listening audits, and efforts to diversify the body across generational lines.

items.title: Motivation for Civic Participation
items.summary: Keshavan described how the 2020 murder of George Floyd motivated her to shift from social observation to active participation in Medford's city government.

items.title: Gentrification and Institutional Relationships
items.summary: The conversation touched on the potential impact of the Green Line extension and the need for Tufts University to provide more resources to the host city.

items.title: Black History Month Programming
items.summary: The West Medford Community Center planned panels featuring City Council leadership and Black artists to discuss a pro-Black agenda and local narratives.

items.title: Perinatal Support and Maternal Health Equity
items.summary: Keshavan highlighted the lack of local perinatal resources, such as diaper pantries and breastfeeding groups, as a critical health equity concern.

items.title: Upcoming Community Panel Announcement
items.summary: Balocca closed the interview by announcing a virtual panel discussion between the West Medford Community Center and Medford City Council leadership.
